headline: Electricity is the movement of electrons—invisible rivers powering our world
universal_truth: Power often flows through invisible channels we take for granted
fun_facts: Electrons in household wiring actually move very slowly—about 0.01 mph—but the energy wave travels near light speed
The human brain runs on about 20 watts of power—less than a dim light bulb
Lightning is nature's electricity: a 300-million-volt discharge lasting a fraction of a second
discussion_questions: What would your life look like without electricity for one week?
What invisible flows of energy power your work and relationships?
How did people connect before electrical communication?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Flip a switch and light appears. Plug in a device and it comes alive. We command electricity so effortlessly that we forget how strange it is. Invisible energy flowing through wires, bringing motion, light, and information. Today, we see what's really happening.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Electricity seems instant—flip the switch, light appears. But electrons in wire move slower than a snail. If electrons are slow, how does turning on a switch at one end of a wire instantly light a bulb at the other end?
cliff.prompt: How does electricity travel so fast if electrons are slow?

options.text: The electromagnetic energy wave travels at near light speed, pushing electrons along
options.response: Yes! It's like pushing one end of a tube of marbles—the energy transfers instantly even though each marble barely moves.

options.text: Special fast electrons carry the energy quickly
options.response: All electrons move slowly—it's the wave of energy that moves fast...

q1.title: Slow Electrons, Fast Energy
q1.script: Individual electrons in your household wiring drift at about 0.01 miles per hour. But the electromagnetic wave that pushes them travels near the speed of light. It's like a stadium wave—each person barely moves, but the wave circles instantly.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Slow Electrons, Fast Energy"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Brain Power
q2.script: Your brain runs on about 20 watts—less than a dim light bulb. Yet it outperforms supercomputers at pattern recognition, language, and creativity. Evolution built the most efficient computer in the known universe, and it runs on the power of a night light.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Lightning: Nature's Discharge
q3.script: Lightning is nature's electricity—300 million volts discharged in a fraction of a second. It heats air to 30,000 Kelvin, five times hotter than the Sun's surface. The thunder you hear is air explosively expanding from that heat.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Like electricity, the most powerful forces in life often flow invisibly. Energy, influence, love—they travel through channels we don't see. Learn to sense the invisible currents that shape your world.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 35. Tomorrow, we'll discover what fire really is. Until then, look at a light switch and appreciate the invisible river of electrons waiting to flow at your command.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Electrical Awareness - Power Audit
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the electricity flowing through your life
growTrack.activity: Count how many electrical devices you use in one hour. Include lights, phones, appliances, everything. Now imagine life without any of them. This exercise builds gratitude for the invisible infrastructure supporting modern life.
